guide.title: Key facts
items: You cannot donate to the province/city or the city/county/district of your registered address. A Suwon resident can donate to every local government except Gyeonggi Province and Suwon (Hometown Love Donation Act, Art. 4①).
Only individuals can donate, not companies. One person may give up to 20 million won a year across all local governments (Art. 8③, raised from 5 million won in 2025).

Each donation earns gift points of up to 30% of the amount, at a rate set by the local government (Enforcement Decree Art. 5①). Points can only be spent on that local government's gifts, last 5 years and cannot be transferred.
Gifts are local products or vouchers usable only in that area. Cash, expensive jewellery and general gift certificates are not allowed (Art. 9②③). You may also donate without taking a gift.
The credit is limited to the tax you owe that year (computed tax) and unused credit is not carried forward (Restriction of Special Taxation Act, Art. 58②). Only the donor can claim it.

Donations made by December 31 count for that year. The record goes to the National Tax Service's electronic donation receipts and shows up in the year-end settlement simplified service. That screen shows only the income tax credit (90,909 won for a 100,000 won donation); the 9,090 won local tax cut comes on top.

Amounts credited as hometown donations cannot also be claimed as ordinary charitable donations (Art. 58③), and paying by card does not count toward the credit card deduction (Enforcement Decree Art. 121-2⑥10-2).

Donating to a declared special disaster area within 3 months of the declaration raises the rate above 200,000 won from 15% to 30% (33% with local tax). For 1 million won the credit rises from 275,999 won to 407,999 won (Art. 58①3, Decree Art. 53-2). This calculator uses the standard rates.

The 130,000 won standard tax credit applies when you claim no special deductions, special credits or rent credit, so people taking the standard credit can still claim the hometown credit (Income Tax Act, Art. 59-4⑨).
Business owners get the tax credit only on the first 100,000 won and expense the rest (Art. 58① proviso). This calculator is for employees.

how.title: How to donate
items: Sign up and log in at Gohyangsarang e-eum (ilovegohyang.go.kr) using a financial certificate, phone or KakaoTalk verification.
Pick a local government and confirm eligibility with your resident registration number. Designated donations to a specific project get the same tax credit.
Choose to receive a gift, then pay by bank transfer, credit card or mobile payment.
Use your points to pick a gift from the local government you supported.
Offline, you can fill in a donation form and pay at any NongHyup Bank or local cooperative branch (about 5,900 nationwide).
Donating right before December 31 leaves no time to fix problems, so give a few days early.

pending.title: Proposed changes (in the National Assembly · not applied)
items: Government 2026 tax reform plan (announced 2026-08-03): from 2027 donations, rates above 100,000 won would depend on the region. For 100,000–200,000 won, the capital area and non-capital metropolitan cities stay at 40% while other non-capital areas go to 50%; above 200,000 won, only disadvantaged non-capital priority areas rise from 15% to 25%.
Bill for a full credit up to 200,000 won (introduced 2026-07-09): would extend the full-credit bracket from 100,000 won to 200,000 won.
Neither had passed as of October 2026 and neither is in the current law (Art. 58, version in force 2026-09-18), so the calculator does not apply them.

hometownDonation.source: Sources: Restriction of Special Taxation Act Art. 58 (amended 2025-12-23, donations from 2026-01-01) and Decree Art. 53-2; Hometown Love Donation Act Arts. 4, 8, 9 and Decree Art. 5; Gohyangsarang e-eum guide. As of October 2026.
